These differential errors do not affect either final answer. q-49386: x=u+1 and dx=du give ∫(u^(6/5)+u^(1/5))du. q-9623: evaluating 2+(x-4)/4-(x-4)²/64 at π gives 1.7739 to four decimal places. q-126875: the first three nonzero terms give 0.5-0.5²/2+0.5³/3=0.416666…, rounding to 0.417. These are the requested Taylor approximations. q-78247 and q-78295: dilation factors are respectively 8 and 1/9, so the matrices are those factors times the identity. q-12043 and q-8054: the diagonal matrices represent dilations by 12 and 3. q-121278: multiplying the signs of x+1 and 2-y gives top row (+,−) and bottom row (−,+). q-149550: y² is positive exactly when y≠0, so negativity requires x>3 and y≠0; current image option 4 depicts the same region as the source solution image, with dashed excluded boundaries. q-50682: f(0)=1, f′(0)=−1/2, and f″(0)=3/4 give 1−x/2+3x²/8. q-83721: f″(3)/2=−1/18. q-116551 and q-116557: setting the quadratic expressions equal to zero yields the asymptote pairs y=±2x and y=±3x.",
